description: "On the shared /data neurico host, API keys may be absent; GPUs are shared/contended; vLLM recipe, cached models, and pitfalls (pkill self-kill, cudnn clash, prompt_logprobs OOM)"

---

Observed 2026-10-14 and 2026-10-16 in neurico research workspaces on this host:
- OPENROUTER_KEY / OPENAI keys were NOT set in the session env (`~/.flamebird/neurico/.env` has it commented out). Resource-finder stage may be skipped (no papers/, datasets/, code/).
- Local models + datasets cached in `/data/transformers/hub` (HF_HOME=/data/transformers): Qwen2.5-{0.5,1.5,3,7,14}B-Instruct safetensors, Qwen3/3.5 family, Llama-3.1-8B, GGUFs; datasets incl. glue(sst2 only), stanfordnlp/sst2, samsum, ag_news, boolq, mmlu. huggingface.co is reachable for extra downloads (curl resolve/main URLs).
- 2026-10-16: 4x RTX A6000 (48GB) present but shared — other users' jobs held ~42GB on 3 GPUs and intermittently grabbed the 4th. Approach that worked: vLLM 0.31 (`uv add "vllm>=0.10"`; unpinned `uv add vllm` resolved an ancient 0.4 build), small `gpu_memory_utilization` (~0.11 ≈ 5GB) for ≤1.5B models on the leftover slices, plus a bash wrapper that polls `nvidia-smi` free memory and retries launch. vLLM checks free mem ≥ util×total at startup.
- 2026-10-14 (no GPU then): llama.cpp multi-server CPU fallback worked; `transformers` CPU generation much slower.
- Pitfalls: `pkill -f <pattern>` inside a Bash call whose text contains the pattern kills the calling shell (find PIDs, kill by PID separately). Leftover `nvidia-cudnn-cu12` 8.x from a failed install breaks flashinfer ("Found 2 libcudnn.so.x") — `uv pip uninstall nvidia-cudnn-cu12`. vLLM `prompt_logprobs` materialises full-vocab logits → OOM on small slices; cap `max_num_batched_tokens` (~1024). Don't edit a bash script while a running loop is executing it.
- Label-restricted log-probs in vLLM: `logprobs_mode="processed_logprobs"` + `allowed_token_ids=label_ids` returns log-softmax renormalised over the labels.

Update 2026-10-16 (inter-model-agreement workspace): 4×A6000 present but shared — other neurico sessions keep each GPU at ~6–10 GB free, fluctuating second to second. What worked:
- `uv venv --python 3.12` (default 3.14 breaks vLLM); pyproject needs `requires-python="==3.12.*"` and `[tool.uv] package=false`.
- vLLM 0.31: no bitsandbytes; set `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0` (JIT build fails); `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`.
- Use pre-quantized 4-bit AWQ/GPTQ checkpoints (~5.5 GB for 8B): Qwen/*-AWQ, hugging-quants Llama-3.1/gemma-2 AWQ-INT4, tiiuae/Falcon3-7B-Instruct-AWQ, solidrust Mistral AWQ, kaitchup Olmo-3/Phi-3 GPTQ.
- Cap gpu_memory_utilization to ~12.5 GB and retry on startup OOM via a scheduler loop; max_model_len 2560, max_num_seqs 64.
- Gated models in /data/transformers/hub (meta-llama Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, google/gemma-7b-it) have weights but no config/tokenizer → unusable; unsloth mirror of Llama-3.1 is complete. Disk /data is ~100% full.

Update 2026-10-16 (few-shot-ordering workspace, 2nd session): a "Begin research execution" prompt can land on a workspace where a prior session already finished most work (REPORT.md exists, background jobs killed at session end). - Startup-race fix that worked: in run_model.py, allocate a placeholder `torch.empty(budget+0.5 GB)` immediately, release it when the vLLM EngineCore child maps `libcuda.so` (poll /proc/<child>/maps every 50 ms). Guard with an env flag (HOLD_PARENT) — vLLM spawns EngineCore by re-importing __main__, so the hold code otherwise runs again in the child. Scheduler threshold: budget + 1.3 GB.
- 16K-token prompts: Qwen2.5-7B-AWQ on a busy shared GPU ≈3k tok/s → 2,880 prompts (18M tokens) took 1h40; budget runs by total prompt tokens. 0.5–1.5B on an idle slice: 5–15 min.

- Long multi-round generation (budget forcing, 12 rounds × up to 2k tokens) on a 100%-util shared GPU is very slow: 7B-AWQ forced arm took ~4 h incl. a ~60 min final answer pass (small KV → ~15 concurrent long contexts). Budget for it, or cut rounds/items for ≥7B.
- My own jobs on the same GPU slow each other badly — don't stack 7B+14B+alt runs on one GPU.
- Two of my queues polling independently launched on the same GPU in the same second and both failed: use ONE queue. - **Retry engine creation in-process** (poll nvidia-smi, size budget = min(max, free−0.35), retry LLM() after failures) instead of relaunching; build prompts AFTER engine init to shrink the race window.
- **Work-stealing pool** (src/worker_pool.py): one thread per GPU launches the highest-priority job whose min budget fits; per-tag flock files prevent duplicates; exit code 75 = "gave up waiting" (not a failure). """Build fixed probe sets, eval sets and training-document pools (model-agnostic text, shared by all runs).

Outputs (datasets/prepared/):
  probes.json   : {"general": [...1000 WikiText-103 test/val paragraphs], "medical": [...300], "code": [...300]}
  train_docs_<domain>.jsonl : training documents (held-out probe/eval docs excluded)
  heldout_<domain>.json     : 100 held-out documents for in-domain loss
  mmlu.json, arc_easy.json  : general-knowledge eval items (fixed random subsets)
"""
import json, os, random
import pandas as pd

HUB = "/data/transformers/hub"
OUT = "datasets/prepared"
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
rng = random.Random(0)

def snap(repo):
    d = f"{HUB}/datasets--{repo.replace('/', '--')}/snapshots"
    return os.path.join(d, os.listdir(d)[0])

# ---- WikiText-103: probes from test+validation, training docs (general control domain) from train
wt = snap("Salesforce/wikitext") + "/wikitext-103-raw-v1/"
def wt_paragraphs(files):
    paras = []
    for f in files:
        for t in pd.read_parquet(wt + f).text:
            t = t.strip()
            if len(t) >= 400 and not t.startswith("="):
                paras.append(t)
    return paras
gen_eval = wt_paragraphs(["test-00000-of-00001.parquet", "validation-00000-of-00001.parquet"])
rng.shuffle(gen_eval)
gen_probes, gen_heldout = gen_eval[:1000], gen_eval[1000:1100]
gen_train = wt_paragraphs(["train-00000-of-00002.parquet"])
rng.shuffle(gen_train)
gen_train = gen_train[:60000]

# ---- Medical: Asclepius synthetic clinical notes (unique notes)
med = pd.read_csv(snap("starmpcc/Asclepius-Synthetic-Clinical-Notes") + "/synthetic.csv").note.drop_duplicates().tolist()
rng.shuffle(med)
med_probes, med_heldout, med_train = med[:300], med[300:400], med[400:40400]

# ---- Code: codeparrot-clean-valid python files (moderate length, not autogenerated)
code = pd.read_parquet("datasets/code/code.parquet")
code = code[(~code.autogenerated) & (code.content.str.len().between(800, 20000))].content.tolist()
rng.shuffle(code)
code_probes, code_heldout, code_train = code[:300], code[300:400], code[400:30400]

json.dump({"general": gen_probes, "medical": med_probes, "code": code_probes}, open(f"{OUT}/probes.json", "w"))
for name, tr, ho in [("general", gen_train, gen_heldout), ("medical", med_train, med_heldout), ("code", code_train, code_heldout)]:
    with open(f"{OUT}/train_docs_{name}.jsonl", "w") as f:
        for t in tr:
            f.write(json.dumps(t) + "\n")
    json.dump(ho, open(f"{OUT}/heldout_{name}.json", "w"))
    print(name, "train docs", len(tr), "chars", sum(map(len, tr)))

# ---- MMLU: 10 questions per subject (57 subjects -> 570), fixed seed
mm = pd.read_parquet(snap("cais/mmlu") + "/all/test-00000-of-00001.parquet")
mm = mm.groupby("subject", group_keys=False).apply(lambda g: g.sample(min(10, len(g)), random_state=0))
mmlu = [{"q": r.question, "choices": list(r.choices), "answer": int(r.answer), "subject": r.subject} for r in mm.itertuples()]
json.dump(mmlu, open(f"{OUT}/mmlu.json", "w"))

# ---- ARC-Easy test: 500 random questions
arc = pd.read_parquet(snap("allenai/ai2_arc") + "/ARC-Easy/test-00000-of-00001.parquet").sample(500, random_state=0)
arc_items = []
for r in arc.itertuples():
    labels = list(r.choices["label"])
    arc_items.append({"q": r.question, "choices": list(r.choices["text"]), "answer": labels.index(r.answerKey)})
json.dump(arc_items, open(f"{OUT}/arc_easy.json", "w"))
print("probes", len(gen_probes), len(med_probes), len(code_probes), "mmlu", len(mmlu), "arc", len(arc_items))
EOF

"""Fine-tune a causal LM on one domain and track representation-geometry drift + forgetting at checkpoints.

At each evaluation step we record (relative to the step-0 = pretrained model):
  * contextual representations of fixed probe texts (mean-pooled hidden states, mid + final layer)
    -> saved to <out>/reps/step_XXXXX.npz (fp16) for offline metrics (neighbourhood preservation,
       isotropy, CKA) computed in src/metrics.py
  * general-knowledge accuracy: MMLU (570 q, 0-shot, letter log-probs) and ARC-Easy (500 q, length-normalised
    choice log-likelihood)
  * WikiText perplexity (general LM ability) and held-out in-domain loss (did fine-tuning learn?)

Usage: python src/train_eval.py --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B --domain medical --method lora --seed 1 --out results/runs/<tag>
"""
import argparse, json, math, os, random, time
import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F
from torch.utils.checkpoint import checkpoint
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer

P = "datasets/prepared"
EVAL_STEPS = [0, 10, 25, 50, 100, 150, 200, 300, 400, 500, 750, 1000, 1250, 1500, 2000, 2500, 3000]


def parse():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--model", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--domain", required=True, choices=["medical", "code", "general"])
    ap.add_argument("--method", default="lora", choices=["lora", "full"])
    ap.add_argument("--steps", type=int, default=3000)
    ap.add_argument("--lr", type=float, default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--bs", type=int, default=4)
    ap.add_argument("--seqlen", type=int, default=512)
    ap.add_argument("--lora_r", type=int, default=64)
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=1)
    ap.add_argument("--probe_len", type=int, default=128)
    ap.add_argument("--eval_bs", type=int, default=16)
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    return ap.parse_args()


def set_seed(s):
    random.seed(s); np.random.seed(s); torch.manual_seed(s); torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(s)


def token_stream(tok, domain, seed, n_tokens):
    """Shuffle training docs (seeded), tokenize, join with EOS, and chunk into fixed-length sequences."""
    docs = [json.loads(l) for l in open(f"{P}/train_docs_{domain}.jsonl")]
    random.Random(seed).shuffle(docs)
    ids, out = [], []
    for d in docs:
        ids.extend(tok(d, add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"] + [tok.eos_token_id])
        if len(ids) >= n_tokens:
            break
    assert len(ids) >= n_tokens, f"not enough tokens: {len(ids)} < {n_tokens}"
    return torch.tensor(ids[:n_tokens])


def chunked_lm_loss(lm_head, h, labels, chunk=1024):
    """Next-token CE computed in token chunks with recomputation, so full-vocab fp32 logits never coexist."""
    h = h[:, :-1].reshape(-1, h.size(-1))
    y = labels[:, 1:].reshape(-1)
    def f(hc, yc):
        return F.cross_entropy(lm_head(hc).float(), yc, reduction="sum")
    tot = 0.0
    for i in range(0, h.size(0), chunk):
        tot = tot + checkpoint(f, h[i:i + chunk], y[i:i + chunk], use_reentrant=False)
    return tot / y.numel()


def backbone_and_head(model):
    m = model.get_base_model() if hasattr(model, "get_base_model") else model
    return m.model, m.lm_head


@torch.no_grad()
def probe_reps(model, tok, texts, layers, max_len, bs):
    """Mean-pooled hidden states (excluding position 0, an attention-sink token) for each probe text."""
    backbone, _ = backbone_and_head(model)
    outs = {l: [] for l in layers}
    for i in range(0, len(texts), bs):
        enc = tok(texts[i:i + bs], return_tensors="pt", padding=True, truncation=True, max_length=max_len,
                  add_special_tokens=False).to("cuda")
        hs = backbone(**enc, output_hidden_states=True).hidden_states
        mask = enc["attention_mask"].clone()
        mask[:, 0] = 0  # right padding -> position 0 is the first real token
        mask = mask.unsqueeze(-1).float()
        for l in layers:
            outs[l].append(((hs[l].float() * mask).sum(1) / mask.sum(1)).cpu())
    return {l: torch.cat(v).numpy() for l, v in outs.items()}


@torch.no_grad()
def seq_logprobs(model, tok, ctxs, conts, bs):
    """Sum log p(cont | ctx) and continuation char length, batched with right padding."""
    _, head = backbone_and_head(model)
    backbone, _ = backbone_and_head(model)
    res = []
    for i in range(0, len(ctxs), bs):
        c_ids = [tok(c, add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"] for c in ctxs[i:i + bs]]
        x_ids = [tok(x, add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"] for x in conts[i:i + bs]]
        seqs = [(c + x)[-1024:] for c, x in zip(c_ids, x_ids)]
        L = max(map(len, seqs))
        inp = torch.full((len(seqs), L), tok.pad_token_id, dtype=torch.long)
        att = torch.zeros_like(inp)
        for j, s in enumerate(seqs):
            inp[j, :len(s)] = torch.tensor(s); att[j, :len(s)] = 1
        inp, att = inp.cuda(), att.cuda()
        h = backbone(input_ids=inp, attention_mask=att).last_hidden_state
        for j, (s, x) in enumerate(zip(seqs, x_ids)):
            n = len(x); s_len = len(s)
            logits = head(h[j, s_len - n - 1:s_len - 1]).float()
            lp = torch.log_softmax(logits, -1).gather(1, inp[j, s_len - n:s_len, None]).sum().item()
            res.append(lp)
    return res


@torch.no_grad()
def eval_mmlu(model, tok, items, bs):
    """0-shot MMLU: compare next-token log-probs of ' A'..' D' after 'Answer:'."""
    _, head = backbone_and_head(model)
    backbone, _ = backbone_and_head(model)
    letter_ids = [tok(" " + L, add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"][-1] for L in "ABCD"]
    correct = []
    for i in range(0, len(items), bs):
        batch = items[i:i + bs]
        prompts = []
        for it in batch:
            subj = it["subject"].replace("_", " ")
            p = f"The following is a multiple choice question about {subj}.\n\n{it['q']}\n"
            p += "".join(f"{L}. {c}\n" for L, c in zip("ABCD", it["choices"])) + "Answer:"
            prompts.append(p)
        enc = tok(prompts, return_tensors="pt", padding=True, add_special_tokens=False).to("cuda")
        h = backbone(**enc).last_hidden_state
        last = enc["attention_mask"].sum(1) - 1
        logits = head(h[torch.arange(len(batch)), last]).float()[:, letter_ids]
        pred = logits.argmax(-1).cpu().tolist()
        correct += [int(p == it["answer"]) for p, it in zip(pred, batch)]
    return correct


def eval_arc(model, tok, items, bs):
    """ARC-Easy, acc_norm: argmax of choice log-likelihood / choice char length."""
    ctxs, conts, owner = [], [], []
    for qi, it in enumerate(items):
        for c in it["choices"]:
            ctxs.append(f"Question: {it['q']}\nAnswer:"); conts.append(" " + c); owner.append(qi)
    lps = seq_logprobs(model, tok, ctxs, conts, bs)
    scores = [[] for _ in items]
    for qi, lp, x in zip(owner, lps, conts):
        scores[qi].append(lp / len(x))
    return [int(int(np.argmax(s)) == it["answer"]) for s, it in zip(scores, items)]


@torch.no_grad()
def eval_ppl(model, tok, texts, seqlen, bs):
    """Token-level mean NLL over held-out documents chunked to seqlen."""
    backbone, head = backbone_and_head(model)
    ids = []
    for t in texts:
        ids.extend(tok(t, add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"] + [tok.eos_token_id])
    n = len(ids) // seqlen
    x = torch.tensor(ids[:n * seqlen]).view(n, seqlen)[:64]
    tot, cnt = 0.0, 0
    for i in range(0, x.size(0), bs):
        b = x[i:i + bs].cuda()
        h = backbone(input_ids=b).last_hidden_state
        for j in range(b.size(0)):
            lg = head(h[j, :-1]).float()
            tot += F.cross_entropy(lg, b[j, 1:], reduction="sum").item(); cnt += seqlen - 1
    return tot / cnt


def main():
    a = parse()
    os.makedirs(f"{a.out}/reps", exist_ok=True)
    set_seed(a.seed)
    lr = a.lr if a.lr is not None else (2e-4 if a.method == "lora" else 1e-5)
    cfg = vars(a) | {"lr": lr, "eval_steps": [s for s in EVAL_STEPS if s <= a.steps], "start": time.ctime()}
    json.dump(cfg, open(f"{a.out}/config.json", "w"), indent=1)

    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(a.model)
    if tok.pad_token is None:
        tok.pad_token = tok.eos_token
    tok.padding_side = "right"
    dtype = torch.bfloat16 if a.method == "lora" else torch.float32
    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(a.model, dtype=dtype).cuda()
    model.config.use_cache = False
    n_layers = model.config.num_hidden_layers
    layers = [n_layers // 2, n_layers]  # hidden_states index: mid layer, final (post-norm) layer

    if a.method == "lora":
        from peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
        model.enable_input_require_grads()
        model = get_peft_model(model, LoraConfig(r=a.lora_r, lora_alpha=2 * a.lora_r, lora_dropout=0.0,
                                                 target_modules=["q_proj", "k_proj", "v_proj", "o_proj",
                                                                 "gate_proj", "up_proj", "down_proj"]))
    model.gradient_checkpointing_enable(gradient_checkpointing_kwargs={"use_reentrant": False})
    params = [p for p in model.parameters() if p.requires_grad]
    n_train = sum(p.numel() for p in params)
    opt = torch.optim.AdamW(params, lr=lr, weight_decay=0.0, betas=(0.9, 0.95))
    warm = 50
    sched = torch.optim.lr_scheduler.LambdaLR(opt, lambda s: min(1.0, (s + 1) / warm))  # constant after warmup

    probes = json.load(open(f"{P}/probes.json"))
    mmlu = json.load(open(f"{P}/mmlu.json")); arc = json.load(open(f"{P}/arc_easy.json"))
    held_gen = json.load(open(f"{P}/heldout_general.json")); held_dom = json.load(open(f"{P}/heldout_{a.domain}.json"))
    stream = token_stream(tok, a.domain, a.seed, a.steps * a.bs * a.seqlen).view(-1, a.seqlen)
    print(f"model={a.model} trainable={n_train/1e6:.1f}M seqs={stream.size(0)} lr={lr}", flush=True)

    autocast = torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16, enabled=(a.method == "full"))
    backbone, head = backbone_and_head(model)
    log = open(f"{a.out}/metrics.jsonl", "a")
    t0, run_loss = time.time(), []

    def evaluate(step):
        model.eval()
        te = time.time()
        with autocast:
            reps = {}
            for name in ["general", "medical", "code"]:
                r = probe_reps(model, tok, probes[name], layers, a.probe_len, a.eval_bs)
                for l, v in r.items():
                    reps[f"{name}_L{l}"] = v.astype(np.float16)
            np.savez_compressed(f"{a.out}/reps/step_{step:05d}.npz", **reps)
            mm = eval_mmlu(model, tok, mmlu, a.eval_bs)
            ar = eval_arc(model, tok, arc, a.eval_bs * 2)
            nll_gen = eval_ppl(model, tok, held_gen, 512, a.eval_bs // 2)
            nll_dom = eval_ppl(model, tok, held_dom, 512, a.eval_bs // 2)
        rec = {"step": step, "mmlu": float(np.mean(mm)), "arc_easy": float(np.mean(ar)),
               "nll_general": nll_gen, "nll_domain": nll_dom,
               "train_loss": float(np.mean(run_loss)) if run_loss else None,
               "elapsed": time.time() - t0, "eval_secs": time.time() - te}
        json.dump({"step": step, "mmlu": mm, "arc": ar}, open(f"{a.out}/reps/items_{step:05d}.json", "w"))
        log.write(json.dumps(rec) + "\n"); log.flush()
        print(json.dumps(rec), flush=True)
        model.train()

    evaluate(0)
    model.train()
    for step in range(1, a.steps + 1):
        x = stream[(step - 1) * a.bs: step * a.bs].cuda()
        with autocast:
            h = backbone(input_ids=x).last_hidden_state
            loss = chunked_lm_loss(head, h, x)
        loss.backward()
        torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(params, 1.0)
        opt.step(); sched.step(); opt.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
        run_loss.append(loss.item())
        if step in EVAL_STEPS:
            evaluate(step)
            run_loss = []
    open(f"{a.out}/DONE", "w").write(time.ctime())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/bin/bash
# Work-stealing worker: claims jobs from a jobs file (one "<tag> <args...>" per line) via atomic mkdir locks.
# Usage: src/worker.sh <gpu> <jobs_file> ; failed jobs are released and retried after a pause.
GPU=$1; JOBS=$2
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
source .venv/bin/activate
export HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 HF_HOME=/data/transformers PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
mkdir -p results/runs results/locks logs/runs
while true; do
  claimed=""
  while read -r tag args; do
    [ -z "$tag" ] && continue
    [ -f results/runs/$tag/DONE ] && continue
    if mkdir results/locks/$tag 2>/dev/null; then claimed=$tag; jargs=$args; break; fi
  done < "$JOBS"
  [ -z "$claimed" ] && { echo "[$GPU] no jobs left"; exit 0; }
  echo "[$GPU] $(date +%T) start $claimed"
  rm -rf results/runs/$claimed
  CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=$GPU python src/train_eval.py $jargs --out results/runs/$claimed > logs/runs/$claimed.log 2>&1
  if [ -f results/runs/$claimed/DONE ]; then echo "[$GPU] $(date +%T) done $claimed"

# Planning: Embedding-Space Drift Under Fine-Tuning

## Motivation & Novelty Assessment

### Why This Research Matters
Domain fine-tuning is the standard way to specialise LLMs, but it causes catastrophic forgetting of general
capabilities. Benchmarking general ability after every checkpoint is expensive, while measuring the geometry of a
model's representations on a fixed probe set is cheap and label-free. If geometric drift (e.g. loss of
nearest-neighbour structure) reliably precedes or tracks forgetting, it could serve as an early-warning monitor
during fine-tuning, and it would tell practitioners how model scale and target domain affect how fast a model
"forgets its pretraining geometry".

### Gap in Existing Work
No literature review or papers were pre-gathered for this workspace (the resource-finder stage was skipped), so
this assessment rests on background knowledge rather than a systematic review. Related work: representation
similarity across fine-tuning (CKA/SVCCA studies of BERT fine-tuning, e.g. Merchant et al. 2020 "What happens to
BERT embeddings during fine-tuning?"), anisotropy of contextual embeddings (Ethayarajh 2019; Mu & Viswanath 2018;
IsoScore, Rudman et al. 2022), and forgetting in LLM continual fine-tuning (Luo et al. 2023; Kalajdzievski 2024
"Scaling laws for forgetting"; Biderman et al. 2024 "LoRA learns less and forgets less"). Gaps: (i) those studies
mostly measure similarity at the end of training, not as a *step-resolved trajectory*; (ii) they rarely relate
local neighbourhood structure (kNN preservation) quantitatively to forgetting of general knowledge; (iii) scale
comparisons within one model family with an identical recipe are rare; (iv) the claim that domain vocabulary
overlap with pretraining data predicts geometric preservation is untested.

### Our Novel Contribution
A step-resolved study (17 checkpoints, 0–3000 steps) of four same-family base models (Qwen2.5 0.5B/1.5B/3B/7B)
fine-tuned with an identical LoRA recipe on medical, code and general (control) text, tracking kNN neighbourhood
preservation, isotropy, CKA, and general-knowledge accuracy (MMLU, ARC-Easy) + general perplexity at every
checkpoint. We test four specific, pre-registered quantitative claims (below) rather than just reporting trends.

### Experiment Justification
- **Exp 1 – Scale × steps (core):** LoRA fine-tuning of 0.5B/1.5B/3B/7B on medical and code text with probe
  evaluation at 17 checkpoints. Needed to test "<50% preservation within 500 steps for sub-1B, 2000+ for 7B".
- **Exp 2 – Isotropy trajectories:** same checkpoints, three isotropy measures (mean pairwise cosine, IsoScore,
  effective rank). Needed to test "isotropy decreases monotonically".
- **Exp 3 – Geometry vs forgetting:** MMLU/ARC-Easy/WikiText NLL per checkpoint, aligned to preservation. Needed to
  test the "60% preservation threshold" early-warning claim (does accuracy start to drop at ~60%? does
  preservation lead accuracy?).
- **Exp 4 – Domain comparison + vocabulary overlap:** medical vs code vs general-text control, plus corpus-level
  measures of overlap with general text (unigram JS divergence vs WikiText, base-model NLL). Needed to test
  "medical preserves more structure than code because of vocabulary overlap".
- **Robustness:** 3 seeds for 0.5B/1.5B (medical, code), multiple k for kNN, two layers (mid, final); if time,
  learning-rate and full-fine-tuning ablations for the small model (method/lr are confounds of "steps").

## Research Question
How fast, in optimisation steps, does fine-tuning destroy the neighbourhood structure and isotropy of a pretrained
LM's representation space, how does that depend on model scale and fine-tuning domain, and does the loss of
neighbourhood structure predict forgetting of general knowledge?

## Hypothesis Decomposition
- **H1 (scale/speed):** kNN@10 neighbourhood preservation (general-text probes, final layer) falls below 0.50
  by step 500 for the sub-1B model (0.5B) and does not fall below 0.50 before step 2000 for 7B.
- **H2 (isotropy):** isotropy decreases monotonically with steps (mean pairwise cosine rises; IsoScore/effective
  rank fall); tested by Spearman ρ(step, metric) and the fraction of monotonicity violations.
- **H3 (early warning):** general-knowledge accuracy (MMLU, ARC-E) is stable while preservation ≥ 0.60 and starts
  declining once it drops below 0.60; i.e. a 0.60 threshold separates "no forgetting" from "forgetting"
  checkpoints, and preservation changes precede accuracy changes.
- **H4 (domain):** medical fine-tuning preserves more structure (higher preservation at matched steps) than code
  fine-tuning; medical text is closer to general text in vocabulary.

Independent variables: model size (0.5/1.5/3/7B), domain (medical/code/general), training step, seed.
Dependent variables: kNN preservation (k=5/10/20), CKA, isotropy metrics, MMLU, ARC-E, NLL on WikiText, domain NLL.

## Proposed Methodology

### Approach
Same base-model family (Qwen2.5 base, shared tokenizer/pretraining data) to isolate scale. LoRA (r=64, α=128, all
linear layers, lr 2e-4, constant after 50 warm-up steps, AdamW β=(0.9,0.95), batch 4×512 tokens, 3000 steps =
6.1M tokens) is used for every size because full fine-tuning of 7B is infeasible on the shared GPUs (only one
GPU slice ≥ 30 GB available); identical recipe across sizes makes "steps" comparable. Representations: mean-pooled
hidden states (positions ≥1, 128-token truncation) of 1000 held-out WikiText-103 paragraphs (general probes) plus
300 medical and 300 code probes, at the middle and final layer.

### Experimental Steps
1. Prepare fixed probe sets, held-out eval texts, MMLU (570 q, 10/subject) and ARC-Easy (500 q) subsets.
2. For each run, evaluate at steps {0,10,25,50,100,150,200,300,400,500,750,1000,1250,1500,2000,2500,3000};
   store representations, item-level accuracy and NLLs.
3. Offline: compute kNN preservation vs step 0, CKA, isotropy; threshold-crossing steps (linear interpolation in
   log-step); relate to accuracy.
4. Corpus analysis: unigram token distribution JS divergence domain↔WikiText, OOV-ish rates, base-model NLL.

### Baselines
- Step 0 (pretrained model) is the reference for all geometric metrics.
- General-text (WikiText) fine-tuning as a control domain: isolates the effect of *being fine-tuned* from the
  effect of *domain shift*.
- Noise floor: preservation between two seeds' runs / bootstrap over probes.

### Evaluation Metrics
- kNN preservation@k: mean over probes of |N_k^base(i) ∩ N_k^t(i)| / k (cosine similarity).
- Linear CKA (global similarity).
- Isotropy: mean pairwise cosine (anisotropy), IsoScore, effective rank (exp of entropy of normalised
  covariance eigenvalues).
- Forgetting: Δ MMLU, Δ ARC-E accuracy vs step 0 (McNemar / paired bootstrap on items), Δ WikiText NLL.

### Statistical Analysis Plan
- Crossing steps with seed variability (3 seeds for 0.5B/1.5B) and bootstrap CIs over probes.
- Paired item-level tests (McNemar exact) for accuracy change vs step 0; bootstrap 95% CIs.
- H3: compare accuracy deltas for checkpoints with preservation ≥0.6 vs <0.6 (Mann–Whitney), plus
  Spearman/Kendall correlation between preservation and Δaccuracy across checkpoints, and a lead/lag check.
- H2: Spearman ρ(step, metric) per run; count monotonicity violations beyond bootstrap noise.
- α = 0.05; Holm correction across the four hypotheses' primary tests.

## Expected Outcomes
H1 supported if 0.5B crosses 0.5 by ≤500 steps and 7B only after ≥2000. H2 supported if all isotropy metrics move
monotonically toward anisotropy. H3 supported if accuracy drops coincide with preservation <0.6 and not before.
H4 supported if medical preservation > code preservation at matched steps, consistently across sizes.

## Timeline and Milestones
Setup+data 30 min; runs ~3–5 h (7B LoRA dominant; shared GPUs); analysis 1 h; report 45 min.

## Potential Challenges
- Shared, contended GPUs (5 GB slices; one ~30 GB slice): queue with retries, small loss chunks, prioritise 7B.
- LoRA vs full FT and fixed lr are confounds for "steps"; documented and partially ablated.
- Probe pooling/layer choice affects metrics: report two layers and several k.

## Success Criteria
All four hypotheses receive a clear supported / refuted / partially supported verdict backed by step-resolved data
for ≥3 model sizes and ≥2 domains, with variance estimates.

How fast, in optimisation steps, does fine-tuning destroy the neighbourhood structure and isotropy of a pretrained
LM's representation space, how does that depend on model scale and fine-tuning domain, and does the loss of
neighbourhood structure predict forgetting of general knowledge?

## Hypothesis Decomposition
- **H1 (scale/speed):** kNN@10 neighbourhood preservation (general-text probes, final layer) falls below 0.50
  by step 500 for the sub-1B model (0.5B) and does not fall below 0.50 before step 2000 for 7B.
- **H2 (isotropy):** isotropy decreases monotonically with steps (mean pairwise cosine rises; IsoScore/effective
  rank fall); tested by Spearman ρ(step, metric) and the fraction of monotonicity violations.
- **H3 (early warning):** general-knowledge accuracy (MMLU, ARC-E) is stable while preservation ≥ 0.60 and starts
  declining once it drops below 0.60; i.e. a 0.60 threshold separates "no forgetting" from "forgetting"
  checkpoints, and preservation changes precede accuracy changes.
- **H4 (domain):** medical fine-tuning preserves more structure (higher preservation at matched steps) than code
  fine-tuning; medical text is closer to general text in vocabulary.

Independent variables: model size (0.5/1.5/3/7B), domain (medical/code/general), training step, seed.
Dependent variables: kNN preservation (k=5/10/20), CKA, isotropy metrics, MMLU, ARC-E, NLL on WikiText, domain NLL.

## Proposed Methodology

### Approach
Same base-model family (Qwen2.5 base, shared tokenizer/pretraining data) to isolate scale. LoRA (r=64, α=128, all
linear layers, lr 2e-4, constant after 50 warm-up steps, AdamW β=(0.9,0.95), batch 4×512 tokens, 3000 steps =
6.1M tokens) is used for every size because full fine-tuning of 7B is infeasible on the shared GPUs (only one
GPU slice ≥ 30 GB available); identical recipe across sizes makes "steps" comparable. Representations: mean-pooled
hidden states (positions ≥1, 128-token truncation) of 1000 held-out WikiText-103 paragraphs (general probes) plus
300 medical and 300 code probes, at the middle and final layer.

### Experimental Steps
1. Prepare fixed probe sets, held-out eval texts, MMLU (570 q, 10/subject) and ARC-Easy (500 q) subsets.
2. For each run, evaluate at steps {0,10,25,50,100,150,200,300,400,500,750,1000,1250,1500,2000,2500,3000};
   store representations, item-level accuracy and NLLs.
3. Offline: compute kNN preservation vs step 0, CKA, isotropy; threshold-crossing steps (linear interpolation in
   log-step); relate to accuracy.
4. Corpus analysis: unigram token distribution JS divergence domain↔WikiText, OOV-ish rates, base-model NLL.

### Baselines
- Step 0 (pretrained model) is the reference for all geometric metrics.
- General-text (WikiText) fine-tuning as a control domain: isolates the effect of *being fine-tuned* from the
  effect of *domain shift*.
- Noise floor: preservation between two seeds' runs / bootstrap over probes.

### Evaluation Metrics
- kNN preservation@k: mean over probes of |N_k^base(i) ∩ N_k^t(i)| / k (cosine similarity).
- Linear CKA (global similarity).
- Isotropy: mean pairwise cosine (anisotropy), IsoScore, effective rank (exp of entropy of normalised
  covariance eigenvalues).
- Forgetting: Δ MMLU, Δ ARC-E accuracy vs step 0 (McNemar / paired bootstrap on items), Δ WikiText NLL.

### Statistical Analysis Plan
- Crossing steps with seed variability (3 seeds for 0.5B/1.5B) and bootstrap CIs over probes.
- Paired item-level tests (McNemar exact) for accuracy change vs step 0; bootstrap 95% CIs.
- H3: compare accuracy deltas for checkpoints with preservation ≥0.6 vs <0.6 (Mann–Whitney), plus
  Spearman/Kendall correlation between preservation and Δaccuracy across checkpoints, and a lead/lag check.
- H2: Spearman ρ(step, metric) per run; count monotonicity violations beyond bootstrap noise.
- α = 0.05; Holm correction across the four hypotheses' primary tests.

## Expected Outcomes
H1 supported if 0.5B crosses 0.5 by ≤500 steps and 7B only after ≥2000. H2 supported if all isotropy metrics move
monotonically toward anisotropy. H3 supported if accuracy drops coincide with preservation <0.6 and not before.
H4 supported if medical preservation > code preservation at matched steps, consistently across sizes.

## Timeline and Milestones
Setup+data 30 min; runs ~3–5 h (7B LoRA dominant; shared GPUs); analysis 1 h; report 45 min.

## Potential Challenges
- Shared, contended GPUs (5 GB slices; one ~30 GB slice): queue with retries, small loss chunks, prioritise 7B.
- LoRA vs full FT and fixed lr are confounds for "steps"; documented and partially ablated.
- Probe pooling/layer choice affects metrics: report two layers and several k.

## Success Criteria
All four hypotheses receive a clear supported / refuted / partially supported verdict backed by step-resolved data
for ≥3 model sizes and ≥2 domains, with variance estimates.

"""Offline geometry metrics for every run: kNN neighbourhood preservation, CKA and isotropy per checkpoint.

Reads results/runs/<tag>/reps/step_*.npz (+ metrics.jsonl) and writes results/all_metrics.csv
(one row per run × step × probe-set × layer, with the run's accuracy / NLL metrics joined in).
"""
import glob, json, os
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import torch

KS = (5, 10, 20)
dev = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() and os.environ.get("METRICS_GPU") else "cpu"


def knn_idx(X, k):
    """Indices of k nearest neighbours by cosine similarity (self excluded)."""
    X = torch.nn.functional.normalize(torch.as_tensor(X, dtype=torch.float64, device=dev), dim=1)
    S = X @ X.T
    S.fill_diagonal_(-np.inf)
    return S.topk(k, dim=1).indices.cpu().numpy()


def preservation(nb0, nb1):
    """Mean fraction of base-model neighbours retained."""
    k = nb0.shape[1]
    return float(np.mean([len(set(a) & set(b)) / k for a, b in zip(nb0, nb1)]))


def linear_cka(X, Y):
    X = X - X.mean(0); Y = Y - Y.mean(0)
    X = torch.as_tensor(X, dtype=torch.float64, device=dev); Y = torch.as_tensor(Y, dtype=torch.float64, device=dev)
    hsic = (X.T @ Y).norm() ** 2
    return float(hsic / ((X.T @ X).norm() * (Y.T @ Y).norm()))


def isotropy(X):
    """Return (mean pairwise cosine, IsoScore [Rudman et al. 2022], effective rank of covariance)."""
    X = torch.as_tensor(X, dtype=torch.float64, device=dev)
    Xn = torch.nn.functional.normalize(X, dim=1)
    n = X.shape[0]
    S = Xn @ Xn.T
    avg_cos = float((S.sum() - n) / (n * (n - 1)))
    Xc = X - X.mean(0)
    # eigenvalues of covariance via Gram matrix (n << d is typical)
    ev = torch.linalg.eigvalsh(Xc @ Xc.T / (n - 1)).clamp(min=0).flip(0)
    p = ev / ev.sum()
    eff_rank = float(torch.exp(-(p[p > 0] * torch.log(p[p > 0])).sum()))
    # IsoScore: variance vector in PCA basis, padded with zeros to ambient dimension d
    d = X.shape[1]
    var = torch.zeros(d, dtype=torch.float64, device=dev); var[:len(ev)] = ev[:d]
    vhat = np.sqrt(d) * var / var.norm()
    delta = (vhat - 1).norm() / np.sqrt(2 * (d - np.sqrt(d)))
    phi = (d - delta ** 2 * (d - np.sqrt(d))) ** 2 / d ** 2
    iso = float((d * phi - 1) / (d - 1))
    return avg_cos, iso, eff_rank


def parse_tag(tag):
    # e.g. q0.5b_lora_medical_s1, q0.5b_full_code_s1, q0.5b_lora_medical_s1_lr5e-4
    parts = tag.split("_")
    return {"model": parts[0][1:].upper(), "method": parts[1], "domain": parts[2], "seed": int(parts[3][1:]),
            "variant": "_".join(parts[4:]) or "base"}


def process_run(rdir, cache):
    tag = os.path.basename(rdir)
    files = sorted(glob.glob(f"{rdir}/reps/step_*.npz"))
    if not files:
        return []
    m = {json.loads(l)["step"]: json.loads(l) for l in open(f"{rdir}/metrics.jsonl")}
    if tag in cache and cache[tag]["n"] == len(files):
        return cache[tag]["rows"]
    base = dict(np.load(files[0]))
    keys = list(base.keys())
    nb0 = {(key, k): knn_idx(base[key], k) for key in keys for k in KS}
    rows = []
    for f in files:
        step = int(f.split("_")[-1].split(".")[0])
        cur = base if step == 0 else dict(np.load(f))
        for key in keys:
            probe, layer = key.split("_L")
            X0, X1 = base[key].astype(np.float64), cur[key].astype(np.float64)
            r = {"run": tag, **parse_tag(tag), "step": step, "probe": probe, "layer": int(layer)}
            for k in KS:
                r[f"pres{k}"] = preservation(nb0[(key, k)], knn_idx(X1, k))
            r["cka"] = linear_cka(X0, X1)
            r["avg_cos"], r["isoscore"], r["eff_rank"] = isotropy(X1)
            r.update({kk: m.get(step, {}).get(kk) for kk in ["mmlu", "arc_easy", "nll_general", "nll_domain", "train_loss"]})
            rows.append(r)
    cache[tag] = {"n": len(files), "rows": rows}
    return rows


def main():
    cache_f = "results/geometry_cache.json"
    cache = json.load(open(cache_f)) if os.path.exists(cache_f) else {}
    rows = []
    for rdir in sorted(glob.glob("results/runs/*")):
        rows += process_run(rdir, cache)
        print(rdir, len(rows), flush=True)
    json.dump(cache, open(cache_f, "w"))
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    df.to_csv("results/all_metrics.csv", index=False)
    print(df.groupby(["run"]).step.max())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Vocabulary overlap of each fine-tuning corpus with general (pretraining-like) text.

General reference = WikiText-103 training paragraphs (a proxy: Qwen2.5's real pretraining corpus is not public).
Measures (on ~2M tokens / ~1.5M words per corpus, Qwen2.5 tokenizer):
  * Jensen-Shannon divergence between token unigram distributions (domain vs WikiText)
  * token mass covered by the 10k most frequent WikiText tokens
  * word-level: fraction of domain word tokens whose lower-cased type occurs in the WikiText sample
Writes results/corpus_stats.json.
"""
import collections, json, re
import numpy as np
from transformers import AutoTokenizer

tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B")

        for d in docs:

content.text: The worker queue can starve 0.5B jobs behind 1.5B jobs that don't fit the small slices; I'll make workers skip jobs whose memory need exceeds the GPU's free memory.

input.command:
cat > src/worker2.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# Work-stealing worker (v2): like worker.sh but only claims jobs whose estimated memory fits the GPU's free memory.
# Usage: src/worker2.sh <gpu> <jobs_file>
GPU=$1; JOBS=$2
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
source .venv/bin/activate
export HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 HF_HOME=/data/transformers PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
mkdir -p results/runs results/locks logs/runs
need_mb() { case "$1" in q0.5b*) echo 2700;; q1.5b*) echo 4700;; q3b*) echo 9500;; *) echo 20000;; esac; }
while true; do
  free=$(nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.free --format=csv,noheader,nounits -i $GPU)
  claimed=""; remaining=0
  while read -r tag args; do
    [ -z "$tag" ] && continue
    [ -f results/runs/$tag/DONE ] && continue
    remaining=1
    [ "$free" -lt "$(need_mb $tag)" ] && continue
    if mkdir results/locks/$tag 2>/dev/null; then claimed=$tag; jargs=$args; break; fi
  done < "$JOBS"
  [ "$remaining" = 0 ] && { echo "[$GPU] no jobs left"; exit 0; }
  [ -z "$claimed" ] && { sleep 30; continue; }
  echo "[$GPU] $(date +%T) start $claimed (free ${free}MB)"
  rm -rf results/runs/$claimed
  CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=$GPU python src/train_eval.py $jargs --out results/runs/$claimed > logs/runs/$claimed.log 2>&1
  if [ -f results/runs/$claimed/DONE ]; then echo "[$GPU] $(date +%T) done $claimed"
  else echo "[$GPU] $(date +%T) FAILED $claimed"; rmdir results/locks/$claimed; sleep 60; fi
done
EOF
chmod +x src/worker2.sh; ps -eo pid,ppid,cmd | grep -E "[w]orker.sh (0|1|3) |[t]rain_eval" | cut -c1-150; ls results/locks

"""Hypothesis tests + figures from results/all_metrics.csv (produced by src/metrics.py).

H1  crossing steps of kNN@10 preservation below 0.5 / 0.6 by model size
H2  monotonicity of isotropy metrics over steps
H3  preservation vs general-knowledge forgetting (0.6 threshold, lead/lag)
H4  medical vs code preservation; vocabulary overlap
Outputs: results/analysis/*.csv|json, figures/*.png
"""
import glob, json, os
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy import stats

os.makedirs("results/analysis", exist_ok=True); os.makedirs("figures", exist_ok=True)
df = pd.read_csv("results/all_metrics.csv")
SIZE = {"160M": 0.16, "410M": 0.41, "0.5B": 0.5, "1.5B": 1.5, "3B": 3.0, "7B": 7.0}
df["size_b"] = df.model.map(SIZE)
df["family"] = np.where(df.run.str.startswith("p"), "Pythia", "Qwen2.5")
df["final"] = df.groupby("run").layer.transform("max") == df.layer
df["gk"] = (df.mmlu * 570 + df.arc_easy * 500) / 1070  # pooled general-knowledge accuracy (1070 items)
base = df[df.step == 0].set_index(["run", "probe", "layer"])
for c in ["mmlu", "arc_easy", "gk", "nll_general"]:
    df["d_" + c] = df[c].values - base.loc[list(zip(df.run, df.probe, df.layer)), c].values
G = df[(df.probe == "general") & df.final].copy()  # primary view: general probes, final layer
G.to_csv("results/analysis/primary_view.csv", index=False)
out = {}
COL = {"medical": "#1f77b4", "code": "#d62728", "general": "#7f7f7f"}


def crossing(steps, vals, thr):
    """First step where the curve goes below thr (linear interpolation in log(1+step)); None if never."""
    steps, vals = np.asarray(steps, float), np.asarray(vals, float)
    for i in range(1, len(steps)):
        if vals[i] < thr <= vals[i - 1]:
            x0, x1 = np.log1p(steps[i - 1]), np.log1p(steps[i])
            return float(np.expm1(x0 + (vals[i - 1] - thr) / (vals[i - 1] - vals[i]) * (x1 - x0)))
    return None


# ---------------- H1: crossing steps
rows = []
for (run, layer), g in df[(df.probe == "general")].groupby(["run", "layer"]):
    g = g.sort_values("step")
    r = {"run": run, "model": g.model.iloc[0], "family": g.family.iloc[0], "method": g.method.iloc[0],
         "domain": g.domain.iloc[0], "seed": g.seed.iloc[0], "variant": g.variant.iloc[0],
         "layer": layer, "final_layer": bool(g.final.iloc[0]), "max_step": int(g.step.max())}
    for m in ["pres10", "pres10_centered"]:
        for thr in [0.5, 0.6]:
            r[f"{m}_cross{thr}"] = crossing(g.step, g[m], thr)
        r[f"{m}_at500"] = float(g[g.step == 500][m].iloc[0]) if (g.step == 500).any() else None
        r[f"{m}_at_max"] = float(g[m].iloc[-1]); r[f"{m}_min"] = float(g[m].min())
    rows.append(r)
cross = pd.DataFrame(rows).sort_values(["family", "model", "domain", "method", "variant", "seed", "layer"])
cross.to_csv("results/analysis/h1_crossings.csv", index=False)
print(cross[cross.final_layer][["run", "max_step", "pres10_at500", "pres10_at_max", "pres10_cross0.5",
                                "pres10_cross0.6", "pres10_centered_at_max"]].to_string())

# Fig 1: preservation trajectories
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(16, 4.6), sharey=True)
for ax, dom in zip(axes, ["medical", "code", "general"]):
    for run, g in G[(G.domain == dom) & (G.variant == "base")].groupby("run"):
        g = g.sort_values("step")
        ls = "-" if g.method.iloc[0] == "lora" else "--"
        alpha = 1.0 if g.seed.iloc[0] == 1 else 0.35
        ax.plot(g.step + 1, g.pres10, ls, marker="o", ms=3, alpha=alpha,
                label=f"{g.family.iloc[0]}-{g.model.iloc[0]} {g.method.iloc[0]}" if g.seed.iloc[0] == 1 else None)
    ax.axhline(0.5, color="k", lw=0.8, ls=":"); ax.axhline(0.6, color="gray", lw=0.8, ls=":")
    ax.axvline(501, color="k", lw=0.6, alpha=0.4); ax.axvline(2001, color="k", lw=0.6, alpha=0.4)
    ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.set_title(f"{dom} fine-tuning"); ax.set_xlabel("training step + 1 (log)")
    ax.set_ylim(0, 1.02); ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
axes[0].set_ylabel("kNN@10 neighbourhood preservation\n(general probes, final layer)")
axes[0].legend(fontsize=7, loc="lower left")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.savefig("figures/fig1_preservation_trajectories.png", dpi=150); plt.close()

# ---------------- H2: isotropy monotonicity
rows = []
for (run, probe, layer), g in df[df.probe == "general"].groupby(["run", "probe", "layer"]):
    g = g.sort_values("step")
    r = {"run": run, "layer": layer, "final_layer": bool(g.final.iloc[0]), "domain": g.domain.iloc[0],
         "model": g.model.iloc[0], "variant": g.variant.iloc[0], "method": g.method.iloc[0]}
    for m, aniso_sign in [("avg_cos", +1), ("isoscore", -1), ("eff_rank", -1)]:
        v = g[m].values
        rho, p = stats.spearmanr(g.step, v)
        d = np.diff(v) * aniso_sign  # >0 means "more anisotropic" at the next checkpoint
        r[f"{m}_rho"] = rho; r[f"{m}_p"] = p
        r[f"{m}_frac_steps_more_aniso"] = float(np.mean(d > 0))
        r[f"{m}_rel_change"] = float((v[-1] - v[0]) / abs(v[0]))
        r[f"{m}_monotone_aniso"] = bool(np.all(d >= 0))
    rows.append(r)
iso = pd.DataFrame(rows)
iso.to_csv("results/analysis/h2_isotropy.csv", index=False)
isof = iso[iso.final_layer]
out["h2"] = {"n_runs": int(len(isof)),
             "n_monotone_more_anisotropic": {m: int(isof[f"{m}_monotone_aniso"].sum()) for m in ["avg_cos", "isoscore", "eff_rank"]},
             "n_net_more_anisotropic": {"avg_cos": int((isof.avg_cos_rel_change > 0).sum()),
                                        "isoscore": int((isof.isoscore_rel_change < 0).sum()),
                                        "eff_rank": int((isof.eff_rank_rel_change < 0).sum())},
             "median_rel_change": {m: float(isof[f"{m}_rel_change"].median()) for m in ["avg_cos", "isoscore", "eff_rank"]}}
print(json.dumps(out["h2"], indent=1))

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(16, 4.4))
for ax, m, lab in zip(axes, ["avg_cos", "isoscore", "eff_rank"],
                      ["mean pairwise cosine (↑ = more anisotropic)", "IsoScore (↓ = less isotropic)",
                       "effective rank (↓ = less isotropic)"]):
    for run, g in G[(G.variant == "base") & (G.seed == 1)].groupby("run"):
        g = g.sort_values("step")
        ax.plot(g.step + 1, g[m] / g[m].iloc[0], marker="o", ms=2, color=COL[g.domain.iloc[0]],
                ls="-" if g.method.iloc[0] == "lora" else "--", alpha=0.4 + 0.1 * np.log1p(g.size_b.iloc[0] * 4))
    ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.set_title(lab, fontsize=10); ax.set_xlabel("step + 1 (log)"); ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
    ax.set_ylabel("relative to step 0")
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
axes[0].legend([Line2D([], [], color=c) for c in COL.values()], list(COL), fontsize=8)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.savefig("figures/fig2_isotropy.png", dpi=150); plt.close()

# ---------------- H3: preservation vs forgetting
# item-level McNemar test of each checkpoint vs step 0 on the 1070 MMLU+ARC items
def items(run, step):
    f = f"results/runs/{run}/reps/items_{step:05d}.json"
    if not os.path.exists(f):
        return None
    d = json.load(open(f)); return np.array(d["mmlu"] + d["arc"])

mc = []
for run, g in G.groupby("run"):
    i0 = items(run, 0)
    for s in sorted(g.step):
        i1 = items(run, s)
        if i0 is None or i1 is None:
            continue
        b, c = int(((i0 == 1) & (i1 == 0)).sum()), int(((i0 == 0) & (i1 == 1)).sum())
        p = stats.binomtest(b, b + c).pvalue if b + c > 0 else 1.0
        mc.append({"run": run, "step": s, "lost": b, "gained": c, "mcnemar_p": p,
                   "sig_decline": bool(p < 0.05 and b > c)})
mc = pd.DataFrame(mc)
G = G.merge(mc, on=["run", "step"], how="left")
G.to_csv("results/analysis/primary_view.csv", index=False)

h3 = G[(G.step > 0)].copy()

ax.legend([Line2D([], [], color=c) for c in COL.values()], list(COL), fontsize=8)
ax.set_title("Domain comparison (all models, seed 1)")

axes[0].set_ylabel("kNN@10 preservation"); axes[0].legend(fontsize=8)

"""Hypothesis tests + figures from results/all_metrics.csv (produced by src/metrics.py).

H1  crossing steps of kNN@10 preservation below 0.5 / 0.6 by model size
H2  monotonicity of isotropy metrics over steps
H3  preservation vs general-knowledge forgetting (0.6 threshold, lead/lag)
H4  medical vs code preservation; vocabulary overlap
Outputs: results/analysis/*.csv|json, figures/*.png
"""
import glob, json, os
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy import stats

os.makedirs("results/analysis", exist_ok=True); os.makedirs("figures", exist_ok=True)
df = pd.read_csv("results/all_metrics.csv")
SIZE = {"160M": 0.16, "410M": 0.41, "0.5B": 0.5, "1.5B": 1.5, "3B": 3.0, "7B": 7.0}
df["size_b"] = df.model.map(SIZE)
df["family"] = np.where(df.run.str.startswith("p"), "Pythia", "Qwen2.5")
df["final"] = df.groupby("run").layer.transform("max") == df.layer
df["gk"] = (df.mmlu * 570 + df.arc_easy * 500) / 1070  # pooled general-knowledge accuracy (1070 items)
base = df[df.step == 0].set_index(["run", "probe", "layer"])
for c in ["mmlu", "arc_easy", "gk", "nll_general"]:
    df["d_" + c] = df[c].values - base.loc[list(zip(df.run, df.probe, df.layer)), c].values
G = df[(df.probe == "general") & df.final].copy()  # primary view: general probes, final layer
G.to_csv("results/analysis/primary_view.csv", index=False)
out = {}
COL = {"medical": "#1f77b4", "code": "#d62728", "general": "#7f7f7f"}


def crossing(steps, vals, thr):
    """First step where the curve goes below thr (linear interpolation in log(1+step)); None if never."""
    steps, vals = np.asarray(steps, float), np.asarray(vals, float)
    for i in range(1, len(steps)):
        if vals[i] < thr <= vals[i - 1]:
            x0, x1 = np.log1p(steps[i - 1]), np.log1p(steps[i])
            return float(np.expm1(x0 + (vals[i - 1] - thr) / (vals[i - 1] - vals[i]) * (x1 - x0)))
    return None


# ---------------- H1: crossing steps
rows = []
for (run, layer), g in df[(df.probe == "general")].groupby(["run", "layer"]):
    g = g.sort_values("step")
    r = {"run": run, "model": g.model.iloc[0], "family": g.family.iloc[0], "method": g.method.iloc[0],
         "domain": g.domain.iloc[0], "seed": g.seed.iloc[0], "variant": g.variant.iloc[0],
         "layer": layer, "final_layer": bool(g.final.iloc[0]), "max_step": int(g.step.max())}
    for m in ["pres10", "pres10_centered"]:
        for thr in [0.5, 0.6]:
            r[f"{m}_cross{thr}"] = crossing(g.step, g[m], thr)
        r[f"{m}_at500"] = float(g[g.step == 500][m].iloc[0]) if (g.step == 500).any() else None
        r[f"{m}_at_max"] = float(g[m].iloc[-1]); r[f"{m}_min"] = float(g[m].min())
    rows.append(r)
cross = pd.DataFrame(rows).sort_values(["family", "model", "domain", "method", "variant", "seed", "layer"])
cross.to_csv("results/analysis/h1_crossings.csv", index=False)
print(cross[cross.final_layer][["run", "max_step", "pres10_at500", "pres10_at_max", "pres10_cross0.5",
                                "pres10_cross0.6", "pres10_centered_at_max"]].to_string())

# Fig 1: preservation trajectories
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(16, 4.6), sharey=True)
for ax, dom in zip(axes, ["medical", "code", "general"]):
    for run, g in G[(G.domain == dom) & (G.variant == "base")].groupby("run"):
        g = g.sort_values("step")
        ls = "-" if g.method.iloc[0] == "lora" else "--"
        alpha = 1.0 if g.seed.iloc[0] == 1 else 0.35
        ax.plot(g.step + 1, g.pres10, ls, marker="o", ms=3, alpha=alpha,
                label=f"{g.family.iloc[0]}-{g.model.iloc[0]} {g.method.iloc[0]}" if g.seed.iloc[0] == 1 else None)
    ax.axhline(0.5, color="k", lw=0.8, ls=":"); ax.axhline(0.6, color="gray", lw=0.8, ls=":")
    ax.axvline(501, color="k", lw=0.6, alpha=0.4); ax.axvline(2001, color="k", lw=0.6, alpha=0.4)
    ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.set_title(f"{dom} fine-tuning"); ax.set_xlabel("training step + 1 (log)")
    ax.set_ylim(0, 1.02); ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
axes[0].set_ylabel("kNN@10 neighbourhood preservation\n(general probes, final layer)")
axes[0].legend(fontsize=7, loc="lower left")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.savefig("figures/fig1_preservation_trajectories.png", dpi=150); plt.close()

# ---------------- H2: isotropy monotonicity
rows = []
for (run, probe, layer), g in df[df.probe == "general"].groupby(["run", "probe", "layer"]):
    g = g.sort_values("step")
    r = {"run": run, "layer": layer, "final_layer": bool(g.final.iloc[0]), "domain": g.domain.iloc[0],
         "model": g.model.iloc[0], "variant": g.variant.iloc[0], "method": g.method.iloc[0]}
    for m, aniso_sign in [("avg_cos", +1), ("isoscore", -1), ("eff_rank", -1)]:
        v = g[m].values
        rho, p = stats.spearmanr(g.step, v)
        d = np.diff(v) * aniso_sign  # >0 means "more anisotropic" at the next checkpoint
        r[f"{m}_rho"] = rho; r[f"{m}_p"] = p
        r[f"{m}_frac_steps_more_aniso"] = float(np.mean(d > 0))
        r[f"{m}_rel_change"] = float((v[-1] - v[0]) / abs(v[0]))
        r[f"{m}_monotone_aniso"] = bool(np.all(d >= 0))
    rows.append(r)
iso = pd.DataFrame(rows)
iso.to_csv("results/analysis/h2_isotropy.csv", index=False)
isof = iso[iso.final_layer]
out["h2"] = {"n_runs": int(len(isof)),
             "n_monotone_more_anisotropic": {m: int(isof[f"{m}_monotone_aniso"].sum()) for m in ["avg_cos", "isoscore", "eff_rank"]},
             "n_net_more_anisotropic": {"avg_cos": int((isof.avg_cos_rel_change > 0).sum()),
                                        "isoscore": int((isof.isoscore_rel_change < 0).sum()),
                                        "eff_rank": int((isof.eff_rank_rel_change < 0).sum())},
             "median_rel_change": {m: float(isof[f"{m}_rel_change"].median()) for m in ["avg_cos", "isoscore", "eff_rank"]}}
print(json.dumps(out["h2"], indent=1))

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(16, 4.4))
for ax, m, lab in zip(axes, ["avg_cos", "isoscore", "eff_rank"],
                      ["mean pairwise cosine (↑ = more anisotropic)", "IsoScore (↓ = less isotropic)",
                       "effective rank (↓ = less isotropic)"]):
    for run, g in G[(G.variant == "base") & (G.seed == 1)].groupby("run"):
        g = g.sort_values("step")
        ax.plot(g.step + 1, g[m] / g[m].iloc[0], marker="o", ms=2, color=COL[g.domain.iloc[0]],
                ls="-" if g.method.iloc[0] == "lora" else "--", alpha=0.4 + 0.1 * np.log1p(g.size_b.iloc[0] * 4))
    ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.set_title(lab, fontsize=10); ax.set_xlabel("step + 1 (log)"); ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
    ax.set_ylabel("relative to step 0")
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
axes[0].legend([Line2D([], [], color=c) for c in COL.values()], list(COL), fontsize=8)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.savefig("figures/fig2_isotropy.png", dpi=150); plt.close()

# ---------------- H3: preservation vs forgetting
# item-level McNemar test of each checkpoint vs step 0 on the 1070 MMLU+ARC items
def items(run, step):
    f = f"results/runs/{run}/reps/items_{step:05d}.json"
    if not os.path.exists(f):
        return None
    d = json.load(open(f)); return np.array(d["mmlu"] + d["arc"])

mc = []
for run, g in G.groupby("run"):
    i0 = items(run, 0)
    for s in sorted(g.step):
        i1 = items(run, s)
        if i0 is None or i1 is None:
            continue
        b, c = int(((i0 == 1) & (i1 == 0)).sum()), int(((i0 == 0) & (i1 == 1)).sum())
        p = stats.binomtest(b, b + c).pvalue if b + c > 0 else 1.0
        mc.append({"run": run, "step": s, "lost": b, "gained": c, "mcnemar_p": p,
                   "sig_decline": bool(p < 0.05 and b > c)})
mc = pd.DataFrame(mc)
G = G.merge(mc, on=["run", "step"], how="left")
G.to_csv("results/analysis/primary_view.csv", index=False)

h3 = G[(G.step > 0)].copy()
hi, lo = h3[h3.pres10 >= 0.6], h3[h3.pres10 < 0.6]
out["h3"] = {"n_ckpt_pres_ge_0.6": int(len(hi)), "n_ckpt_pres_lt_0.6": int(len(lo)),
             "mean_d_gk_pres_ge_0.6": float(hi.d_gk.mean()) if len(hi) else None,
             "mean_d_gk_pres_lt_0.6": float(lo.d_gk.mean()) if len(lo) else None,
             "frac_sig_decline_pres_ge_0.6": float(hi.sig_decline.mean()) if len(hi) else None,
             "frac_sig_decline_pres_lt_0.6": float(lo.sig_decline.mean()) if len(lo) else None}
if len(hi) and len(lo):
    out["h3"]["mwu_p"] = float(stats.mannwhitneyu(hi.d_gk, lo.d_gk).pvalue)
rho, p = stats.spearmanr(h3.pres10, h3.d_gk); out["h3"]["spearman_pres_vs_dgk_all"] = [rho, p]
rho, p = stats.spearmanr(h3.pres10, h3.d_nll_general); out["h3"]["spearman_pres_vs_dnllgen_all"] = [rho, p]
# per-run: first significant decline vs preservation at that moment
per = []
for run, g in G.groupby("run"):
    g = g.sort_values("step")
    sig = g[g.sig_decline == True]
    first = int(sig.step.iloc[0]) if len(sig) else None
    # sustained decline: first step after which every later checkpoint is below step-0 accuracy
    below = (g.d_gk < 0).values
    sustained = next((int(s) for k, s in enumerate(g.step) if s > 0 and below[k:].all()), None)
    rr, pp = stats.spearmanr(g.pres10[g.step > 0], g.d_gk[g.step > 0])
    per.append({"run": run, "first_sig_decline_step": first,
                "pres10_at_first_sig_decline": float(g[g.step == first].pres10.iloc[0]) if first is not None else None,
                "sustained_decline_from_step": sustained,
                "pres10_at_sustained": float(g[g.step == sustained].pres10.iloc[0]) if sustained is not None else None,
                "d_gk_at_max_step": float(g.d_gk.iloc[-1]), "d_mmlu_at_max": float(g.d_mmlu.iloc[-1]),
                "d_arc_at_max": float(g.d_arc_easy.iloc[-1]), "d_nll_general_at_max": float(g.d_nll_general.iloc[-1]),
                "pres10_cross0.6": crossing(g.step, g.pres10, 0.6), "within_run_spearman": rr, "within_run_p": pp,
                "max_step": int(g.step.max())})
per = pd.DataFrame(per); per.to_csv("results/analysis/h3_per_run.csv", index=False)
print(per.to_string())
print(json.dumps(out["h3"], indent=1))

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 4.6))
for run, g in G[G.variant == "base"].groupby("run"):
    g = g.sort_values("step")
    for ax, y in zip(axes, ["d_gk", "d_nll_general"]):
        ax.plot(g.pres10, g[y] * (100 if y == "d_gk" else 1), marker="o", ms=3, alpha=0.6,
                color=COL[g.domain.iloc[0]], ls="-" if g.method.iloc[0] == "lora" else "--")
for ax, lab in zip(axes, ["Δ general-knowledge acc (pp, MMLU+ARC-E)", "Δ WikiText NLL (nats/token)"]):
    ax.axvline(0.6, color="k", ls=":", lw=1); ax.axhline(0, color="gray", lw=0.8)
    ax.set_xlabel("kNN@10 preservation (general probes, final layer)"); ax.set_ylabel(lab); ax.invert_xaxis()
    ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
axes[0].legend([Line2D([], [], color=c) for c in COL.values()], list(COL), fontsize=8)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.savefig("figures/fig3_preservation_vs_forgetting.png", dpi=150); plt.close()

# ---------------- H4: domain comparison (matched model/seed/method/variant/step)
piv = G[G.step > 0].pivot_table(index=["model", "method", "variant", "seed", "step"], columns="domain", values="pres10")
if {"medical", "code"} <= set(piv.columns):
    pv = piv.dropna(subset=["medical", "code"])
    diff = pv.medical - pv.code
    out["h4"] = {"n_matched_ckpts": int(len(pv)), "mean_diff_med_minus_code": float(diff.mean()),
                 "frac_med_gt_code": float((diff > 0).mean()),
                 "wilcoxon_p": float(stats.wilcoxon(diff).pvalue) if len(pv) > 5 else None}
    # run-level (last common step) comparison, one value per model/method/variant/seed
    last = pv.reset_index().sort_values("step").groupby(["model", "method", "variant", "seed"]).tail(1)
    last["diff"] = last.medical - last.code
    last.to_csv("results/analysis/h4_last_common_step.csv", index=False)
    out["h4"]["per_run_last_common_step"] = last.round(4).to_dict("records")
    for m in ["pres10_centered", "cka", "d_gk", "d_nll_general"]:
        pm = G[G.step > 0].pivot_table(index=["model", "method", "variant", "seed", "step"], columns="domain",
                                       values=m).dropna(subset=["medical", "code"])
        out["h4"][f"mean_diff_{m}"] = float((pm.medical - pm.code).mean())
        out["h4"][f"wilcoxon_p_{m}"] = float(stats.wilcoxon(pm.medical - pm.code).pvalue) if len(pm) > 5 else None
out["corpus_stats"] = json.load(open("results/corpus_stats.json"))
# in-domain probes: how much do medical/code probe neighbourhoods move under each fine-tuning domain?
dom_probe = df[df.final & (df.step > 0)].groupby(["run", "probe"]).apply(
    lambda g: g.sort_values("step").pres10.iloc[-1], include_groups=False).unstack()
dom_probe.to_csv("results/analysis/probe_set_preservation_at_max_step.csv")
print(dom_probe.round(3).to_string())
print(json.dumps({k: v for k, v in out.get("h4", {}).items() if k != "per_run_last_common_step"}, indent=1))

# Fig 4: domain comparison at matched steps
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4.6))
for (model, method, variant), g in G[(G.seed == 1) & (G.variant == "base")].groupby(["model", "method", "variant"]):
    for dom in ["medical", "code", "general"]:
        h = g[g.domain == dom].sort_values("step")
        if len(h):
            ax.plot(h.step + 1, h.pres10, color=COL[dom], ls="-" if method == "lora" else "--", alpha=0.6)
ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.set_xlabel("step + 1 (log)"); ax.set_ylabel("kNN@10 preservation"); ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
ax.legend([Line2D([], [], color=c) for c in COL.values()], list(COL), fontsize=8)
ax.set_title("Domain comparison (all models, seed 1)")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.savefig("figures/fig4_domain_comparison.png", dpi=150); plt.close()

# Fig 5: preservation vs model size at fixed steps (Qwen2.5 LoRA, seed 1)
q = G[(G.family == "Qwen2.5") & (G.method == "lora") & (G.variant == "base")]
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 4.2), sharey=True)
for ax, dom in zip(axes, ["medical", "code"]):
    for s, c in zip([100, 500, 1000, 2000, 3000], plt.cm.viridis(np.linspace(0, 0.9, 5))):
        h = q[(q.domain == dom) & (q.step == s)].groupby("size_b").pres10.agg(["mean", "std", "count"]).reset_index()
        if len(h):
            ax.errorbar(h.size_b, h["mean"], yerr=h["std"].fillna(0), marker="o", color=c, label=f"step {s}", capsize=3)
    ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.set_xlabel("model size (B params, log)"); ax.set_title(dom); ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
    ax.axhline(0.5, color="k", ls=":", lw=0.8)
axes[0].set_ylabel("kNN@10 preservation"); axes[0].legend(fontsize=8)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.savefig("figures/fig5_preservation_vs_size.png", dpi=150); plt.close()

json.dump(out, open("results/analysis/summary.json", "w"), indent=1, default=float)
